title: Free quotient Grassmannians and their projective Plücker embedding
statement:
For any scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and integers $N\geq0$ and $0\leq r\leq N$, the functor on $S$-schemes sending $T$ to isomorphism classes of surjections $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus N}\twoheadrightarrow Q$, where $Q$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus r}$, is represented [def-pc-representable-functor] by an $S$-scheme $G_S(N,r)$ with a universal quotient. Formation of this scheme and quotient commutes with arbitrary base change. For $0<r<N$, taking the top exterior power of the quotient defines the Plücker closed immersion
$$G_S(N,r)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_S.$$
For $r=0$ or $r=N$, $G_S(N,r)=S$. Thus in every case $G_S(N,r)\to S$ is H-projective [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), and the quotient convention preceding it; projective Plücker embedding as recalled in Grothendieck, Bourbaki Expose 221, proof of Theorem 3.2 preceding Lemma 3.3, printed p.261. Archival Expose 221 PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Assume $0<r<N$. Take the explicitly defined integer determinant locus $X$, its closed immersion $j$ and its affine charts from [lem-sfb-plucker-determinant-locus-charts]. The transition and gluing theorem [lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing] supplies the quotient $q_X$. Applying [lem-sfb-plucker-chart-classifying-bijection] to this quotient gives the natural quotient-class bijection and identifies $j$ with its top exterior-power map, including its coordinate sections.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable); assembly of the three extracted determinant-coordinate arguments

proof.text: For arbitrary $S$, define $G_S(N,r)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ and pull back $q_X$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $S$-maps from $T$ into this scheme are exactly maps $T\to X$ together with the given $T\to S$. [lem-sfb-plucker-chart-classifying-bijection] identifies these naturally with all required quotients on $T$. This proves representability and universality. For $S'\to S$, an $S'$-map $T\to G_S(N,r)\times_SS'$ is likewise precisely an $S$-map $T\to G_S(N,r)$ with the given map $T\to S'$. Hence it represents the quotient functor over $S'$, with the pulled-back quotient. [lem-pc-representable-unique] gives the unique quotient-preserving isomorphism with $G_{S'}(N,r)$. This argument proves arbitrary base change directly and does not use the flat-only base-change clause of the cited Proj theorem.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable) and definition-grassmannian immediately following it; arbitrary base change from the representing bijection and fibre-product universal property

proof.text: Base change $j$ along $\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_S\to\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_{\mathbf Z}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] the resulting map is a closed immersion. The fibre-product universal property identifies its source with $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X=G_S(N,r)$; its target is the specified projective space by [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The determinant-line and section identities of [lem-sfb-plucker-chart-classifying-bijection] identify this map, including its line quotient, with the top exterior-power construction on the universal quotient. Consequently it is the required Plücker embedding, and [def-kun-projective] gives H-projectivity.

source.place: Tag 01N0 (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj); base change of closed immersions; explicit Plücker-coordinate argument of Steps 2–9

proof.text: For $r=0$ the quotient is necessarily the zero module and has exactly one isomorphism class. For $r=N$, in any local frame the surjection is square; at each point its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is a surjective square matrix, so its determinant is nonzero in the residue field and hence a unit in the local ring. Its adjugate gives a local inverse, and uniqueness glues these inverses. Thus $q$ itself identifies $Q$ with $\mathcal O_T^N$, giving again one quotient class. In both cases $S$ represents the functor, with its evident universal quotient, and arbitrary pullback preserves it. Finally $\mathbf P^0_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[t]$ has the single covering chart $D_+(t)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, since its degree-zero localization is $\mathbf Z$; hence $\mathbf P^0_S=S$. The identity is a closed immersion, so $S\to S$ is H-projective by [def-kun-projective]. This includes $N=0$, empty bases and empty test schemes.
